senses: as used in context to describe the experience of social drinking: having a drink, etc.
la:noun:poculum.html:
pōcŭlum (contr. pōclum, ; ; ), i, n.
from root po-, pot; Gr. πίνω, v. potus
.
Lit., a drinking-vessel, a cup, goblet, bowl, beaker (class.; syn.: calix, cyathus): et nobis idem Alcimedon duo pocula fecit, Verg. E: 3, 44: poculum grande,: magnis poculis aliquem invitare,: exhaurire poculum,to empty,; so, ducere,: siccare,: poscunt majoribus poculis (sc. bibere),out of goblets,: stans extra poculum caper,i.e. in relief,; cf. .—Prov.: eodem poculo bibere,i. e. to undergo the same sufferings,.—
Transf.
A drink, draught, potion (mostly poet.): si semel poculum amoris accepit meri,: salsa pocula,sea-water,: pocula sunt fontes liquidi,: amoris poculum,i. e. a philter,; also, desiderii,: prae poculis nescientes,through drunkenness,: pocula praegustare,: poculum ex vino,.—
A drinking-bout, a carouse (class.): in ipsis tuis immanibus poculis,; cf.: is sermo, qui more majorum a summo adhibetur in poculis,while drinking,.—
A draught of poison, alicui poculum dare, ; ; .
